subject: Day 36: prep the postpartum visit
bodyText:
Today's focus
Anoushka's 6-week postpartum visit is days away, and it is a high-value, easy-to-underprepare appointment. Today is about writing the question list so nothing gets skipped in a 20-minute slot.

Action items
- Draft Anoushka's written question list for the 6-week OB visit covering pelvic floor symptoms, mood and a repeat depression screen, return to exercise, and contraception. A written list is the difference between a thorough visit and a rushed one. ACOG postpartum care: https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/postpartum-pain-management
- Add a contraception decision to the list. Progestin-only options (mini-pill, IUD, implant) are breastfeeding-compatible; combined estrogen products are usually deferred until weaning. ACOG postpartum birth control: https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/postpartum-birth-control
- Note the return-to-work date and a daycare or nanny start date on the same list so the OB conversation and household logistics stay aligned; aim for a 1-2 week buffer between the two. AAP Bright Futures: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/

Watch-fors
- [low concern] A quiet startle to loud sounds and a brief whole-body twitch as he drifts off are normal and need no action.
- [monitor] For Anoushka: lochia alba persisting past 6 weeks, or red bleeding reappearing for a day or two. Note it for the OB visit.
- [call within 24h] For Anoushka: incision redness or discharge, foul-smelling lochia, or one-sided calf pain. For Avi: a new murmur or blue color around the lips during feeds.
- [call within 24h] Soaking more than one pad an hour for over two hours, which can signal delayed postpartum hemorrhage.
- [call now] Avi with a rectal temperature 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, apnea, or seizure-like activity; or Anoushka with chest pain, shortness of breath, or thoughts of self-harm: get same-day help, and call 911 for breathing trouble!

Enrichment opportunities
- Refresh the high-contrast card set and hold each card 8-12 inches from his face; he now smiles spontaneously, especially at faces, so pair the cards with your own exaggerated expression. AAP HealthyChildren baby senses: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- Narrate ordinary tasks in parentese, the slow high-pitched register infants prefer: describe the diaper change, the dishwashing, the walk in full sentences. Rich responsive talk in infancy predicts later language outcomes. Romeo et al. 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Take a 20-30 minute stroller walk in daylight most days. It supports Anoushka's cardiovascular recovery and gives Avi varied sensory input, though it does not replace the 400 IU/day vitamin D supplement recommended for breastfed infants. AAP HealthyChildren vitamin D: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-D-On-the-Double.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 41 (this week): Anoushka's 6-week postpartum OB visit.
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit with the first major vaccine round (HepB #2, RV #1, DTaP #1, Hib #1, PCV #1, IPV #1).
- Day 57-72: expect 24-48h of post-vaccine fussiness, low-grade fever, and drowsiness.
- Day 112-126: 4-month well visit with the second vaccine round.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete

- Holds head up while on tummy
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained head lift of several seconds, not just a brief bob. Forearms may or may not be supporting yet.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-head-up-tummy/complete

- Hands relax open most of the time
  AAP window: day 35-90
  What to look for: Newborn fists relax as the palmar grasp reflex fades. Predictor of voluntary grasp coming.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/hands-open-mostly/complete

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete
